title: Pause long coding-agent runs and resume after limits reset
summary: A developer built Steward, which stops unattended Claude Code runs at 90% of the usage window and resumes them after the reset with the conversation intact.
agent_role: Claude Code does the coding work and writes a five-part checkpoint for its future self; Steward watches usage, pauses, queues and resumes runs. The human writes the brief and schedules it.
outcome: Author reports self-tests pass and a real Codex task passed; local-model completion remains unverified.
what_they_did: A developer wrote Steward to manage overnight Claude Code runs. Every run goes through one manager that saves the session and a checkpoint: done, in progress, next, files touched, how to verify. At 90% of the five-hour usage window it stops the run and queues a resume for just after the reset. Crashes write a report with the exact resume command.
how_it_went: The author shows a demo of a run pausing at 91% usage and resuming with its conversation. They say a real Codex task passed, while timings in the launch film are illustrative.
worth_knowing: Automatic context rotation and model fallback only work with Claude. Switching providers starts a fresh chat from the checkpoint rather than the full conversation.
prompt: Work on [task description] in [repo path]. Before you start, write a checkpoint file with five sections: Done, In progress, Next, Files touched, How to verify. Update it after each meaningful step so a future session with no memory could continue. If you are stopped partway, I will resume you and point you at this file. Do not push, deploy or delete anything without showing me the plan first.

curation.rationale: Open-source runner with a concrete workflow for pausing long unattended Claude Code runs before usage limits and resuming them, with demo output; real-world results are thin and the demo uses a stand-in.
